data.long_meaning: Rufinus is derived from the Latin word ‘rufus’, meaning red, dark, or good man. In Christian tradition, Rufinus is the name of several saints and martyrs, including a 4th-century theologian and translator who played a significant role in the spread of early Christian thought. The name Rufinus carries the meaning “Red, dark, or good man” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rufinus usually hope their child will grow to embody red, dark, or good man and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Rufinus' name holds a deep cultural significance in the Christian tradition, as it has been attributed to numerous saints and martyrs throughout history. One of the most notable figures with this name was Rufinus of Aquileia (c. 345-410 AD), a Roman philosopher, theologian, and translator who played a vital role in the transmission of early Christian thought from Greek and Syriac sources into Latin. He translated several important works, including those of Origen and Evagrius Ponticus, which significantly influenced the development of Latin Christianity.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Rufinus holds a spiritual significance as it carries the meaning of 'red' or 'good man' and is associated with several saints and martyrs in the Christian tradition. The 'red' in the name could be symbolic of the blood of Christ, and the name could be a reminder of the sacrifices and martyrdom of the early Christian believers. Moreover, the name 'Rufinus' emphasizes the importance of learning and knowledge in spiritual growth, as seen through the example of St. Rufinus of Aquileia, who played a significant role in the transmission of early Christian thought from Greek and Syriac sources into Latin. This demonstrates that spiritual enlightenment and intellectual robustness go hand in hand in the Christian faith.
